chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the carrier and the employee, he said: 'His sweat should not dry up until you give him his wages.'
ai.seo_question: When should an employer pay a worker's wages according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Hisham ibn al-Hakam, underscores the juristic principle of hastening payment in labor contracts to prevent exploitation. The metaphor of 'sweat not drying' serves as a vivid indicator of immediacy, reflecting the Shia emphasis on fulfilling financial rights (huquq) with precision and fairness. It is frequently cited in fiqh discussions regarding the distinction between agreed-upon wages and the timing of disbursement.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, 
from Abu Abdullah(a.s.)
regarding the carriers and the employees, having said: ‘His sweat should not dry up until you give him his wages’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who has said the following: “About the case of porters and a man working for hire, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
You must pay him before his perspiration dries up.’”
